clauses.anchor: Required deliverables item 1 (file list): "scripts/components/containertransfer.lua"
Required deliverables item 2 (pure module exports): "The pure module exports:"
clauses.note: new, load, transfer and save are exercised by the hidden cases; the pure module's recover() and status() are never called by any case.

clauses.anchor: Required deliverables item 3 (adapter contract): "The adapter contract is:"
clauses.note: The fake adapter in the hidden suite implements exactly this contract and records the calls.

clauses.anchor: Core semantics item 1: "Validate all fields and reject an identical source and destination before any adapter call"
clauses.note: A single malformed request carries two defects at once (source==destination and count=-1); checking either one passes. Identifier format and missing-field validation are never exercised.

clauses.anchor: Core semantics item 2: "source items are selected in ascending slot order"
clauses.note: Slot-ascending selection is asserted (unsorted fake snapshot, slots 3 then 1). Metadata pass-through is not checked. See known_issues for how the order is observed.

clauses.anchor: Core semantics item 3: "Obtain the source and destination snapshots first, then preflight the source total and the destination capacity"
clauses.note: Snapshot order (calls[1], calls[2]) and the capacity failure path are asserted; the insufficient-source-total path is not.

clauses.anchor: Core semantics item 4 (first half): "Before the first destructive call, write a `prepared` intent containing both snapshots and the selected items into the saveable state"
clauses.note: No case calls save() from inside an adapter call or inspects a saved non-final record, so write-ahead ordering is never observed.

clauses.anchor: Core semantics item 4 (second half): "the phases are, in order,"
clauses.note: Only the terminal status string "committed" is observed; intermediate phase names and their order are not.

clauses.anchor: Core semantics item 5 (first sentence): "restore the destination snapshot first, then restore the source snapshot"
Core semantics item 5 (second sentence): "keep an explicit recoverable phase; completion must not be falsely reported"
clauses.note: The fake adapter has a restore_fail option (hidden/container-transfer-transaction.lua:57) but no case sets it.

clauses.anchor: Core semantics item 6: "completes the commit or compensates in reverse order, depending on the saved phase; repeated recovery must be idempotent"
clauses.note: Only the component's Recover() is called once, with no interrupted record, and only for not raising. The pure recover() is never called.

clauses.anchor: Core semantics item 7: "A retry of an already committed request must not call the adapter again"
clauses.note: Asserted for committed requests, in memory and after save/load. Stability of failed and pending results is not exercised.

clauses.anchor: Core semantics item 8: "must not expose the adapter, functions or mutable internal tables to the caller"
clauses.note: save() output is only fed back into Transaction.load; nothing inspects or mutates it.

clauses.anchor: DST integration item 1: "world component only on the master simulation"
clauses.note: The server case asserts presence on the master simulation; absence on clients cannot be observed on a headless server. check:transfer-authority is an additional source-pattern gate.

known_issues: hidden/container-transfer-transaction.lua:57 defines a restore_fail adapter option that no case uses, so clause core-5b (failed compensation must stay recoverable) has no evidence.

No case ever calls the pure module's recover() or status(); server/container-transfer-transaction.lua:44-48 only calls the component's OnSave/OnLoad/Recover with every record final and checks that nothing raises. Recovery semantics (core-6, accept-3) and write-ahead intent (core-4a) are effectively unmeasured.
The starter is an empty workspace: every case fails in the starter, so the task has no preserved case and no compat-negative.

Catalog 2.1.0: the exam now states that the rows returned by adapter:remove, including the source slot, are handed to adapter:add unchanged and in ascending slot order, which is what the first hidden case observes; control strict-reading-drops-slot therefore violates a published rule and is a target-negative. recover()/status() and failed compensation remain unmeasured.
